coordination.selected_lane: SQLite WAL runtime safety / release gating
coordination.reason: Fresh target/main activity showed V17/V18 effect-provenance and ClayCode lanes were already under active concurrent repair. SQLite WAL safety had no current competing work and affects authoritative UnifiedDB continuity plus release recovery semantics.

internal_evidence.finding: Real Hostinger Ubuntu WAL receipt: Python 3.12.3, SQLite 3.45.1, WAL enabled, multi-connection writer/checkpoint behavior measured.

Real self-hosted target-VPS run: SQLite 3.45.1, WAL active, release gate BLOCK; bounded canary completed 2495 writes and 465272 checkpoints over two checkpointer processes in 2 seconds, all workers exit 0, integrity_check=ok, corruption_observed=false. Null race result is diagnostic only and is explicitly forbidden from proving safety.

external_evidence.source: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging: The WAL-Reset Bug
external_evidence.finding: SQLite documents a rare corruption race likely present in upstream 3.7.0 through 3.51.2, fixed in 3.51.3+, requiring WAL mode plus two or more connections in different threads/processes writing/checkpointing concurrently; ordinary organic reproduction is difficult.
3.51.3 explicitly fixes the WAL-reset database corruption bug.

external_evidence.source: Ubuntu USN-8565-1 and Noble package index
external_evidence.finding: Current Ubuntu 24.04/Noble security package is SQLite 3.45.1-1ubuntu2.7. Visible current USN fixes concern other 2026 SQLite issues; semantic version/package number alone is not accepted as proof that the WAL-reset fix is or is not backported.

hypothesis: Frank v0.1 needs a fail-closed SQLite WAL-reset release gate because its authoritative state plane uses WAL on a runtime whose upstream SQLite semantic version is inside SQLite's documented affected range.
strongest_counterhypothesis: The target is safe despite the upstream-affected semantic version because Ubuntu has backported the exact WAL-reset fix, or Frank's actual connection/checkpoint topology makes the necessary concurrent reset race unreachable.
counterhypothesis_status: OPEN; requires exact downstream source/build provenance or a machine-checked runtime topology exclusion. A clean stress canary is insufficient.

implementation.delta: Added fail-closed upstream-version/WAL guard plus bounded disposable race canary.
Added real self-hosted Ubuntu execution and persisted receipt.
Refined gate so upstream semantic version is risk evidence rather than a claim that a distro build is definitely unpatched.
Extended target receipt to collect dpkg package versions, Python _sqlite3 extension path, linked libraries and sqlite3 CLI version for downstream provenance adjudication.

out_of_box_experiment.design: Disposable WAL database with one writer process plus two aggressive checkpoint processes alternating PASSIVE/RESTART/TRUNCATE for two seconds on the real target runner.
out_of_box_experiment.result: NO_CORRUPTION_OBSERVED; 2495 writes; 247355 + 217917 checkpoint calls; all worker exit codes 0; final integrity_check ok.
out_of_box_experiment.interpretation: NEGATIVE_RESULT_DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY. This does not refute SQLite's documented tight-timing race and cannot promote release safety.

architecture_delta.rule: If Frank's authoritative SQLite state uses WAL and runtime upstream version is in the documented affected range, fail closed until one of three independent conditions is proven: upstream-fixed runtime, exact downstream/vendor patch provenance for the WAL-reset fix, or machine-checked topology exclusion of the necessary concurrent write/checkpoint race.
architecture_delta.anti_goodhart: Repeated clean stress runs cannot substitute for version/patch/topology evidence because the upstream race is explicitly difficult to reproduce organically.
architecture_delta.rollback: Guard is additive and uses disposable DBs only; remove/revert test/workflow commits if a superior accepted safety mechanism replaces it.
